newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Ousted Sierra Leone minister wants military action.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Sierra Leone minister wants military action.

text.p: Sierra Leone's ousted foreign minister said on Thursday she believed that only military action could reverse a widely condemned coup that toppled elected civilian president Ahmed Tejan Kabbah.

"It think it has got to the stage where force must be used," Shirley Gbujama told Reuters by telephone from the Nigerian capital Abuja, where she met General Sani Abacha, the military ruler of the regional giant.
"It is regrettable, the stage at which we are is not a time for dialogue. People have tried all kinds of dialogue and have spent five weeks trying and it didn't have any effect," she said.

Foreign ministers from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) decided on June 26 to use dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the coup leaders and their rebel allies to restore Kabbah.

But they also retained the option of military force should a negotiating committee of representatives of Nigeria, Ghana, Guinea, Ivory Coast and the Organisation of African Unity and ECOWAS secretariat fail to make headway after two weeks.
Gbujama said Abacha had promised what assistance he could as ECOWAS chairman.

"We were here in Nigeria to express gratitude to the head of state for the fact that Nigeria has stuck its neck out for us so far," said Gbujama, who was accompanied by Patricia Kabbah, the wife of Sierra Leone's ousted president.
The commander of Nigerian-led ECOMOG troops in Sierra Leone, Major-General Victor Malu, said on Tuesday they had the capacity to drive out the coup leaders if they did not reinstate Kabbah.
Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on June 2 and Nigerian soldiers were in turn attacked by Sierra Leone forces and their Revolutionary United Front rebel allies.
